The apply_template returned a tuple with a list of SMILES strings? It shows "(('CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1',),)". So the result is a tuple containing a tuple with one SMILES string: 'CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1'.

Thus the precursors list is a single precursor? But the reaction likely splits into two precursors: the nitro aromatic and something else? However the template may produce only one precursor (the nitro version) because the other part is unchanged? Actually the product is a complex molecule with a nitro group reduced to amine. The reverse reaction (retro) would replace amine with nitro, giving the nitro precursor. The other part (the rest of molecule) remains same. So the precursor list likely contains the same molecule but with nitro group instead of amine. So the precursor SMILES is 'CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1'.

Thus we need to return list of lists where each inner list contains SMILES of each precursor. Since only one precursor, inner list with that SMILES.

Thus final answer: [["CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1"]]

Check formatting: need double quotes inside outer list. Provide exactly as string.
